svg.title: How much of a one-tonne release remains over 100 years
svg.desc: Curves of the share of a one-off release still in the air over 100 years. HFO-1234yf, lifetime 12 days, vanishes almost at once. Methane, lifetime 11.8 years, is mostly gone within 30 to 40 years. Nitrous oxide, 109 years, falls to about 40%. Carbon dioxide drops quickly at first as oceans and plants take some up, then levels off: about 40% remains after 100 years and about a fifth lasts for millennia.
svg.text: What is left of one tonne, year by year
Share of a one-off release still in the air. Lifetimes from IPCC AR6; CO₂ uses the carbon-cycle fit from IPCC AR5 (illustrative).
